title: India Plans New Framework To Bring Startups Into Government Procurement
excerpt: Speaking at the National Startup Awards 6.0 curtain-raiser, DPIIT officials said procurement relaxations for startups already exist but are under-used, and that a new framework is being prepared with three other ministries.
body:
• DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia said the government is working with other agencies to use public procurement to give startups early access to demand.
  • Additional Secretary Ateesh Kumar Singh said relaxations under the General Financial Rules already exist, but uptake is weak because of information asymmetry, and a new framework is being prepared with the Finance, Public Enterprises and MSME ministries.
  • India has more than 2.5 lakh startups, with more than half in tier-3 and smaller towns, according to DPIIT.
  • For startup founders: applications for the National Startup Awards 6.0 are open from October 27 to November 20, 2026, and DPIIT-recognised startups can already use GeM Startup Runway exemptions from prior experience, prior turnover and earnest money deposit requirements.

The government is working to use its own buying to promote startups, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia said on Tuesday at the curtain-raiser for the National Startup Awards 6.0. Bhatia said private companies also need to do more to engage startups and bring them into their supply chains.

"We are also working with other agencies to see how government procurement can also be better used for promoting startups by providing them with at least early access to demand."

Relaxations exist, uptake does not

DPIIT Additional Secretary Ateesh Kumar Singh said facilities for startups in public procurement already exist in the form of relaxations under the General Financial Rules, and that various agencies have issued circulars intended to make the pathway into government procurement easier. The problem, he said, is that partaking of those benefits remains a challenge.

https://x.com/EconomicTimes/status/2115269171781235174

Singh attributed much of that gap to information asymmetry. One part of the problem is telling founders what is available, he said; the second is helping them actually use it. DPIIT is working with various ministries, including the Department of Finance, Public Enterprises and MSME, on the existing system. "This is ongoing work and we will come up with a new framework," he said.

That account is consistent with the channels Startup India already describes on its official procurement guidance page. DPIIT-recognised startups can register on the Government e-Marketplace through the GeM Startup Runway using their recognition number, list products and services for government departments, and claim exemptions on prior experience, prior turnover and earnest money deposit requirements. The page also describes trial orders, through which a department can test a new product and give the startup feedback, and access to tenders published on the Central Public Procurement Portal.

The awards that framed the announcement

The remarks were made at the launch of the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards, run by DPIIT under the Startup India initiative. According to the DPIIT announcement reproduced by India Education Diary, NSA 6.0 covers 20 sectoral categories and three special categories: women-led startups, startups from the north-eastern region, and a newly introduced student innovator and aspiring entrepreneur award.

Winning startups across the 20 sectoral categories and the two startup-focused special categories will be eligible for a cash prize of Rs 25 lakh per category, subject to the award guidelines. The student award carries a total prize pool of Rs 25 lakh across four sub-categories. Beyond money, the awards are intended to provide mentorship, investor engagement, market access, industry partnerships and visibility. Applications opened on October 27, 2026 and close on November 20, 2026, through the Startup India portal.

Why procurement matters for founders

For a young company, a government order does work that a grant does not: it is revenue, a reference customer and evidence for the next buyer. That is the logic behind Bhatia's phrase "early access to demand" and behind the push to get private firms to open their supply chains as well. The constraint DPIIT identified is practical rather than legal. The relaxations are on paper, but a founder in a smaller town who does not know they exist, or cannot navigate the tender that is supposed to honour them, gets no benefit from them. Singh said more than half of India's startups are now in tier-3 and smaller towns, which makes that information gap a national issue rather than a metro one.

What's next

DPIIT has not given a date for the new procurement framework, and Singh described the work as ongoing across ministries. Founders do not need to wait for it to use what already exists: DPIIT recognition, GeM registration and the Startup India procurement guidance are available now, and the NSA 6.0 application window closes on November 20, 2026. The measure of the promised framework will be whether uptake of the existing relaxations rises, not whether another circular is issued.
